items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: I think it was, uh, Bill Strickland's orchestra, if you know that name.

ctx.x: Tony Earne. Oh, which one of the two that you wrote the words for? If you knew, and why? That's right, if you knew.

And I wrote the verse to Sweet Substitute, but I didn't claim it, I think I should claim it. I think he should claim it. Oh, yeah. It's a good one. He would, uh, yeah, it's getting a little popularity. Mm-hmm. But, uh, funny, funny thing about it, I say he, he nominated me, I said, well, I said, get Sidney Martin, I said, the, the first thing started on those songs was, uh, was a tune that he wrote for a clarinet player that he wanted to record with. Here? Yes. I don't know that played in an orchestra, and I…
